questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to train as a war reporter for the BBC
A war reporter's addictions and mental illness
The history of wars in Africa since the 1990s
How soldiers recover after coming home from war
questions.why: They hear about BBC war correspondent Fergal Keane, who worried he was addicted to war and lived with PTSD.

questions.q: What did reporting from war zones give Fergal Keane?
options: A huge rush of adrenaline found nowhere else
A lot of money and a quiet life
A feeling of calm and inner peace
Many famous friends around the world
questions.why: Neil says it gave him a massive rush of adrenaline, something he couldn't get anywhere else.

questions.q: Where did Fergal first see violence in his career?
options: In Iraq
In Rwanda
In Belfast
In Lebanon
questions.why: He had seen violence since the early days of his career covering the fighting in Belfast.

questions.q: What did Fergal do after he began having nightmares of Rwanda?
options: He went to see a psychiatrist at once
He stopped working for the BBC
He moved back to Ireland
He kept working and turned to alcohol
questions.why: He says he didn't go to a psychiatrist; he kept doing the job and turned to booze.

questions.q: What does Fergal say about his drinking before Rwanda?
options: He was already an alcoholic, but coping
He never drank at all before Rwanda
He only drank a little at parties
He had stopped drinking years before
questions.why: He says he was an alcoholic long before Rwanda, but a 'functioning' one.

questions.q: How does Fergal describe the way his mental health got worse?
options: It happened suddenly after one event
It got worse only when he stopped working
It was a slow, steady wearing away
It was caused by a single nightmare
questions.why: He says 'it's not dramatic, it's a slow, steady erosion' that ended in a breakdown.

questions.q: How did Fergal feel when he was diagnosed with PTSD?
options: Angry with his doctors for waiting
Relieved that it had a name
Ashamed and embarrassed about it
Surprised and confused by the news
questions.why: He says, 'Relief, I think. You know, there's a name to this.'

questions.q: What does Mobeen Azhar suggest about Fergal after the diagnosis?
options: He retired from reporting immediately
He was cured almost straight away
He started a new career in teaching
His addiction kept pulling him back
questions.why: He says you might expect Fergal to stop, but 'that's not how addiction works'.
